clauses.evidenceLine: CLOSED 2026-09-22. The embedding half always held; the REFERENCES half did not, and the reason was structural: on a runner with no JDK and no `../lokalized-java`, the parity report's oracle-derived fields were CARRIED from the record with **nothing to carry them against**. CI was embedding the report against a RECORD of the references rather than against the references. `measurements/reference-runtime-lock.json` is plan 8.4's missing file — it did not exist, `find` returned zero of that name across all four trees — and it pins BOTH halves the clause names that were unpinned: the JDK (vendor, version, build string, plus a sha256 over the distribution's own `release` file) and the Java reference (version and commit). CLDR and IANA are pinned by the spec repo's locks, which CI checks out. `check:reference-lock` compares the shipped report against the lock, needs NEITHER the JDK nor the Java checkout, and is in `verify` and CI in verify's order — the CI-parity gate caught the order mismatch on the first attempt. Where the JDK IS present the lock is additionally re-derived from it; where it is absent that is skipped and SAID to be skipped. **TWO DIVERGENCES FROM 8.4 ARE RECORDED IN THE LOCK RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER.** The plan pins Eclipse Temurin and the reference is Amazon Corretto 21.0.11 — blocker B8, the maintainer's. And 'immutable image digest' presumes a container this project does not use, so no image digest is invented; the distribution digest is recorded under its own name, `releaseFileSha256`, so it cannot be read as the thing the plan asked for.

clauses.ablation: Seventeen, all firing with a named red, control clean both sides, against test/publish-workflow.test.js: id-token granted workflow-wide; an ambient push: trigger; the INLINE on: [workflow_dispatch, push] form; workflow_call: added; npm ci inside the credentialed job; a checkout inside it; a repository script run inside it; --provenance dropped; the publish job no longer declaring needs:; the second digest check removed; a digest comparison made non-fatal; an input interpolated into a ONE-LINE run: body; a stored NODE_AUTH_TOKEN; the dist-tag guard removed; contents: write on the build job; npm run verify moved after the pack step; and `npm publish` given no tarball argument, which would publish the DIRECTORY and so run lifecycle scripts inside the OIDC environment while bypassing the supplied digest. The last two of those fired only after the rules themselves were repaired — see the evidence line. PINNING (M-R S23), all firing, controls clean both sides — against `publish.yml`: one reference reverted to `@v4`; one of its two setup-node steps on a different commit; an abbreviated 7-hex SHA; the reader keeping the comment as part of the value; the reader stripping a # inside quotes; the rule seeing no references. Against every workflow: one CI checkout reverted to `@v4`; CI's setup-node on a different commit from publish's (reds ONLY the cross-workflow rule); a NEW workflow file using a tag; a job-level reusable workflow on a branch — which goes GREEN when the job-level read is removed, so that read is load-bearing; and a census that sees nothing (reds the census floor). THE POST-PUBLISH REPORT (2026-09-24). Two independent reviews broke two versions of the rule before this one: the first read one step and passed reads placed anywhere else; the second read the loop's SHAPE and passed eight wrong edits, one of them the rc.2 failure itself (drop `|| true` and the first E404 ends the step). The rule now EXECUTES the report step under GitHub's shell flags against a stand-in npm, with `curl` and `wget` failing, and holds the structure around it. Measured against every mutation both reviews wrote plus four of mine, re-anchored where the step's wording had since moved: all 37 distinct wrong edits fail — among them the rc.2 shape in its own step, in the Publish step and in another downstream job; `npm show`, `npm --silent view`, a quoted subcommand, a read in a command substitution, after an apostrophe, an escaped quote or a heredoc; a bare `curl` or `wget`; each way of breaking the loop (a failed read made fatal, the deadline reset, shortened or never true, the sleep dropped, the loop never run, the step always passing); the report under `continue-on-error`, behind the publish environment, or no longer after the publish; and the digest check moved into the report or after `npm publish` — while all six legitimate forms pass: `needs` quoted or as a block list, a read inside a shell function, a `for` loop inside the retry loop, an install in the report job, and the report job placed above the publish job in the file.
clauses.evidenceLine: CLOSED 2026-09-24 BY A REAL PUBLISH, which is the only thing this clause ever waited on. `lokalized@1.0.0-rc.2` was published through `.github/workflows/publish.yml` (run 36024984063, dispatched against `feature/m0` at d754c98), and the registry records an attestation for it. Read from the registry, not inferred from the run: `dist.attestations` names `https://registry.npmjs.org/-/npm/v1/attestations/lokalized@1.0.0-rc.2` with predicate `https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1`; that SLSA statement's `buildDefinition.externalParameters.workflow` is repository `https://github.com/lokalized/lokalized-js`, path `.github/workflows/publish.yml`, ref `refs/heads/feature/m0`; its resolved dependency is git commit `d754c9813110e30e7ba7d7f7dae5aad35b500429`; its builder is `https://github.com/actions/runner/github-hosted` and its invocation `.../actions/runs/36024984063/attempts/1`. The subject digest (sha512 `5e718375…251d6b`) equals the sha512 of the tarball the maintainer verified locally before dispatching (sha256 `702833b0…35afd4b7`, the digest typed into the run), and npm's own shasum `ec808ce5…` equals that tarball's sha1. And the registry records WHO published: rc.2's `_npmUser` is `GitHub Actions` <npm-oidc-no-reply@github.com> with `trustedPublisher: {id: "github", oidcConfigId: "oidc:2950fc18-…"}`, where rc.1's is the maintainer's own account with no `trustedPublisher` — npm's record of an OIDC trusted-publisher exchange rather than a token. So the bytes on the registry are the verified bytes, built by this workflow from this commit, published with no stored token. The run itself showed FAILED, and not because of the publish: its last step asked the registry for the new version seconds after the PUT, got E404 "No match found for version 1.0.0-rc.2", and had no retry on that first read. The registry showed the version about five minutes later. The check is now a job of its own, `report`, downstream of the publish and holding no credential, because GitHub re-runs jobs rather than steps and re-running the publish job would publish again. It reads the registry every 30 seconds until a read finishes past ten minutes, with npm's own retries off, and one `npm view --json` read per poll tells an attested version, a version without an attestation, a version not yet visible and no usable answer apart. `test/publish-workflow.test.js` RUNS that step against a stand-in npm — a version that appears late must pass on the read that finds it, and each of the other three must fail within bounds, naming the answer — and requires the publishing job to read the registry nowhere, exactly one step after it to do so, in a job with no credential, environment, condition or continue-on-error, and a deadline of at least 450 seconds (the registry serves the package document with max-age=300). The same day every action in both workflows moved off its Node 20 build, which GitHub had started flagging on every job: checkout v7.0.1, setup-node v7.0.0, upload-artifact v7.0.1, download-artifact v8.0.1, each resolved from its tag to a commit through the API and each `action.yml` read as `runs.using: node24`. What follows is the record as it stood before the publish. THE MACHINERY EXISTS AND THE CLAUSE STILL DOES NOT CLOSE, which is the honest state: plan 9.1 wants PUBLICATION to use provenance/OIDC, and no publication has used it. 1.0.0-rc.1 went out by hand from a laptop with no provenance and those bytes are immutable. What is in place as of 2026-09-22, after a 62-agent adversarial review (58 findings, 22 CONFIRMED / 35 REPAIRED / 1 REFUTED) replaced the 2026-09-21 hand review that had died on API 529: `.github/workflows/publish.yml` publishes by exchanging a GitHub OIDC token for a scoped npm credential with NO stored token anywhere, in TWO JOBS. The split is the security property and the review is what produced it: `id-token: write` is JOB-wide and GitHub exports the OIDC request variables to every step of that job, while npm`s exchange (lib/utils/oidc.js:63-142) needs nothing else — so the single-job draft ran an esbuild install script, a second repository`s install and all of verify beside a credential that can publish as the owner. The credentialed job now downloads a tarball, re-checks its digest and runs one command; publishing a TARBALL executes no lifecycle script at all (lib/commands/publish.js:99 and :215 gate on spec.type === `directory`, libnpmpack/lib/index.js:19 gates prepack the same way), so it runs no repository and no dependency code, and that is gated by an action allowlist plus an npm-subcommand allowlist. CORRECTED, having been stated backwards here since 2026-09-21: --provenance is now PASSED. npm`s auto-enable at oidc.js:144-168 sits entirely inside a try/catch that only logs, so every way it can miss leaves provenance unset and publishes anyway — it FAILS OPEN. With the flag, ensureProvenanceGeneration throws EUSAGE inside buildMetadata, awaited at libnpmpublish/lib/publish.js:44, before the PUT at :54; and the flag costs nothing in authentication because the token exchange at oidc.js:113-142 is outside the isDefaultProvenance guard. Both halves re-read from the installed npm before the reversal was taken. `npm pack` is byte-REPRODUCIBLE here, which is what lets the workflow refuse bytes whose sha256 the releaser did not supply — now checked in BOTH jobs, the second check meaning what reaches the registry is the byte sequence a person verified whatever the build job did. It closes when a real publish runs through it and the registry reports an attestation. TWO halves are NOT ours: the trusted publisher must be registered on npm against this exact filename (`npm trust github lokalized --repo lokalized/lokalized-js --file publish.yml`), which needs the maintainer`s account; and workflow_dispatch does not register until the file is on the DEFAULT branch (master), which no static rule over the file can observe — it is recorded in the workflow header instead.
